payload.claim: This line trusts `outcome.attempts` as the row's effort count, but for a `RATE_LIMITED` outcome the value is always 0 regardless of how much of the repair loop actually ran. `saffron/cell/session.py`'s `RateLimited` handler (~2308-2323) builds its `CellOutcome` with `spent_usd=ledger.task_spend(task_id)` — explicitly rolled up from the ledger because, per its own comment, 'every turn recorded its own attempt before the rate limit was raised' — but never sets `attempts`, so it silently falls back to the dataclass default of 0. A task that burned several real gate-suite attempts before hitting the provider ceiling will now show '0 att' on the index this diff creates, understating exactly the kind of task (`RATE_LIMITED` is one of the eight states §6 calls out as needing the operator) the feature exists to surface, and `sort_key`'s `-line.attempts` tiebreak will rank it as if less work were sunk into it than tasks that did less. New tests in `tests/test_task.py` never catch this because they hand-construct `CellOutcome(attempts=1, ...)` rather than driving the real `session.py` path that produces a `RATE_LIMITED` outcome.
